Nearly nine years ago on this website I took a dive into the Marxist concept of Basis und Überbau, 'Base and the Superstructure'. This concept – arguably one of the most profound, subtle and useful ideas that Marx came up with – has been largely ignored by his followers, who, it seems, have been more interested in fomenting unrest and revolution than doing a bit of deep thinking.

The ignorance and stupidity of the GenZ kids currently demonstrating in support of their demands took me back those nine years.

Marx's insight can be stated very simply. The means of production form the base on which the culture of a society rests. Loosely rephrased in modern, non-Marxist terminology: the technologies available in our society determine our culture (in the very broadest sense of that word, including the way we think and the way we speak).

items.title: Introduction to Curvature
items.label: Small Web
items.excerpt:
A curve can remain the same length while its direction changes. Draw a horizontal line on paper and wrap the paper around a cylinder. The ink keeps its length. Follow it around the cylinder and its tangent rotates in the plane of the circular cross-section. The first fundamental form measures the paper's local lengths and angles. Curvature measures what happens to the direction.

On a circle of radius \(R\), an arc of length \(\Delta s\) turns the tangent by \(\Delta\theta=\Delta s/R\). Thus a large circle changes direction more slowly than a small one. Curvature is the limit of turning per arc length:

The subscript denotes the signed curvature of an oriented plane curve. As you travel along the oriented curve, a left turn of the tangent counts positive and a right turn counts negative. Arc length is measured in metres, so curvature has units of inverse metres.

items.title: Debian: Modernizing iperf/iperf3 and introducing fireperf
items.label: Small Web
items.excerpt:
Recently I spend some time on modernizing the packaging of the Internet Protocol bandwidth measuring tools iperf and iperf3 in Debian, as well as uploading fireperf to Debian.

Previously, src:iperf only built iperf. If you wanted to run an iperf server, you had to do it on your own, i.e. there was no systemd service for that.

Apart from tidying the Debian package, src:iperf now builds the new iperf-client and iperf-server packages, the latter contains the systemd and ufw integration. iperf-server runs with a dynamic systemd user and systemd service hardening.

The iperf package is now a transitional package, that also cleans up any leftovers from before the package split into iperf-client and iperf-server (e.g. when upgrading from trixie to forky).

For historical reasons, iperf2 is packaged in debian as iperf, not iperf2. Now the iperf packages have provides for iperf2, iperf2-client, and iperf2-server respectively (so they can be installed by these names too).

When I feel flattened , algorithmic feeds and (gaming) engagement loops are the likely culprits. It’s not the smartphone that’s the culprit, though the ease with which I can grab it and end up scrolling without realizing it is startling. It’s the same, flat shape of what they’re providing me.

To live in the modern world is to be pulled in all directions. The rush of trends, with some new, hot topic being discussed, keeps us frantically busy; the smartphones we carry make sure that we never forget (but also never truly remember) anything; the algorithmic environment ensures that we never have a moment where content is not being offered to us. We can call this problem ‘fragmentation’: our mental lives are increasingly disunified, and we become a collection of more-or-less disconnected fragments.

— Jared Henderson, Attention Is Love

I don’t need to throw every feed behind a bag of asceticism. I don’t have to throw my phone in the river. But maybe leave the phone in…

items.label: Blogs
items.excerpt:
🫧 Open on Bubbles

I completed one of my AII level 2 exams for more than a month. The examination results should be out after two weeks of the exam. I am now preparing for the fourth subject in this certification. Lately, I find myself checking the portal for my results on a daily basis. The exam department only told me that the examination results will be release when it is ready. I feel apprehensive about my results. If I failed, I have to re-do the subject. I do not expect myself to fail the exam as I have studied for it. Yet the uncertainty has affected my concentration to focus on my current paper's preparation.

I am a classic text-box case of someone worrying over nothing. Knowing how I feel and doing something about it are two different matters. Knowing is the start of change. The change will not be immediate, but it is the beginning.

items.title: Preparing the earth for a persimmon tree
items.label: Q&A
items.excerpt:
I have an enormous aloe plant (about 6 feet tall, 5 feet across) that we are taking out and replacing with a persimmon tree. I'm wondering if there is something we should do between the aloe coming out and the tree going in to prepare the earth to make the tree more likely to succeed.

Given the size of the aloe, I'm expecting that it'll have a pretty big root structure that we won't be able to get access to (there is cement around 1/2 of the planting area). We have chickens and could set them up in the spot to turn over the earth after the aloe comes out. We could add compost, plant a temporary cover crop, just let it rest for a season to give the roots time to decompose, or just put the persimmon tree in right away and hope for the best.

Where I live doesn't hit freezing, but does get a lot of rain in the winter.

Any thoughts on how to prepare the earth for the new tree?

items.title: The Wonder Years
items.label: General
items.excerpt:
Roger Rosenblatt writes heartfelt essays about life and aging for the New York Times:
I Want To Hold Her Hand. /

Why Old People Cry. /

The World Is a Room With a Piano Waiting to Be Played. /

Thoughts Near the End of a Life.

"At the age of 6, I was on vacation with my parents in Westport, Conn. The day of our arrival, I went off for a walk by myself. I was always doing that, to my parents' dismay. And I came upon a large, beautiful house with a sunroom with glass walls so that I could see a Steinway concert grand in the middle of the floor.

The door was open. I went in and started playing, eventually looking up to see a princess-like woman..."

"...standing beside the piano and smiling. We chatted. She took me back to the rented house. My mother was appalled, and she apologized for my bold behavior. No need, said the woman. It was a pleasure to see how innocent and unafraid I was. "Yes," said my mother. "That's how he is. He thinks the world is a room with a piano in it waiting…

items.title: Small portion of damaged gutter = replace the entire house's gutters??
items.label: Q&A
items.excerpt:
Part of a tree fell on my parents' roof, damaging a portion of gutter. A gutter installer says that the only right way to fix this is to replace the gutters all the way around the house. Can that possibly be right? Details below.

The tree didn't damage the roofing itself, but it did cause some of the gutter to get a little bent up and detached from the roof. The damaged area happens to include a downspout and occurs at a roof corner. I reckon about 3' to 5' of gutter length on each side of the corner (so maybe 8' total length) is affected.

I've had a hard time finding any companies that do gutter repair/installation work. The one company I managed to get to look at the situation determined that it would be necessary to replace the gutters all the way around the house's roof in order to properly fix this. The reasoning is this: the roof is a hip style roof, so that the gutter is continuous all the way around the roof; there are no terminations in the gutter. Replacing a portion of…

items.excerpt:
I just started a new blog where I can post about the process of developing software and tech in general. My first proper article is Runtime Quality Requires Humans which is about the limitations of trying to use AI coding with complex systems. I built a new site because I was tired of dealing with ads and paywalls on sites like Medium.

This was also an experiment in using the Astro web framework to make a complex static site, which worked out really well. items.title: Feed the Scorchpot [$14.99] [Strategy] [Windows] [macOS]
items.label: Gaming
items.excerpt:
You struck a deal with a dragon: twenty years of protection for twenty years of dinner service. The island thrives under the beast's watchful eye, as long as the meals keep coming.

Every year, the dragon wakes up hungrier. You roll dice to work your island, harvest ingredients, fuse them into recipes, and cook them down in the Scorchpot — the pot you keep full or end up in. Get the meal right and you prosper. Get it wrong and you're smoke.

Build farmsteads, shrines, and harbors across your hex-grid island, each one changing how the board pays out. The best runs start with a handful of tiles and end with a machine that buries the dragon in food. Then the odds tighten, the dragon turns picky, and you tear the whole thing down and rebuild while it's on fire.

Feed the Scorchpot, keep the dragon happy, and outlast the contract.

Cook cleverly, plan badly, or just roll with it — the dragon doesn't care how you win, only that you feed the beast on time. And yes, you can pet the…
